model_rules.description: The open Revit file is the one the work order names.
Every room number in the contract exists in the model.
The contract and the approved drawings have not changed since the work order was compiled.
The open file is the Draft 2 save-as, not the Draft 1 file.
No room has zero area.
No two rooms share a number.
Room numbers in the model equal the room board.
Room colour fills use the standard palette.
No foundation, electrical, plumbing or structural sheet in a Draft 2 set.
After a wall, stair or size change every room is still enclosed.

After the phase that moves walls, each room whose shape a decision changes matches its approved drawing within the tolerance set on this check. It is a whole-room shape tolerance, not the 1 in casework standard.
model_rules.source: spec amendment A12; 0.25 ft is the initial value (ruling 2026-11-11)

model_rules.description: The model's warning count has not risen.

Every placed or swapped door and window is in the wall the approved drawing puts it in, and sits where it was drawn: along that wall and on its centreline, each within the tolerance set on this check. The checker works the wall out itself from the drawing and the model, not from what the build phase says: it is the one wall behind the wall face the mark sits on, no further back than half the wall's thickness plus the host search margin set on this check. When it finds no such wall, or more than one, the check is reported as not run, never as passed. It does not check the swing side or the hand of a door.
Every opening carries a type mark and the marks check is clean.
No two casework solids overlap.
Built casework sits within 1 inch of the approved 2D drawing.
No casework crosses a door, window or appliance.
Every face of every built family has a material.
Each counter cutout equals its sink bowl, the sink is centred, the rim is under the slab.
No countertop has a built-in backsplash.
Toilets have 15 inches to each side and 21 inches in front.
Shower tile walls are cut around every opening in the host wall.
Niches are real cuts in the wall.
Each bath is one room.
A finish floor is present on both sides of every door.
No slab is left without a finish floor.
Ceiling heights are measured and match the notes.
One material per role across the house.
No material is named after the project.
Every material's texture files sit in the shared library folders.
The roof sits correctly on the walls.
Overhang dimensions do not collide with the grid lines.
The driveway is a split of the site surface, not an overlay.
The conceptual-site-plan note is on the site sheet unless a survey was given.
The sheet set matches the list for this draft stage.
Everything on every sheet sits inside the page outline.
Tags are text only.
Door and window schedules are on the dimension plan.
The final model and sheet checks are clean.
The PDF of the full set exists.

Before a build phase changes an element that already exists, the element is within the tolerance set on this check of where the approved drawing shows it. If it has moved further than that since the drawing was approved, the phase stops instead of changing it.
model_rules.source: was a constant in the work-order compiler; made a check by ruling 2026-11-11 (flag 45, spec amendment A46)
